newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker in sluggish trade.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed slightly lower in light trading on Monday, pressured by local and trade selling amid a background of ample supplies," dealers said.
"It was very quiet," said one trader. "Most people just think there's plenty of juice around."
He said local selling was seen in September, while trade selling was noted mainly in the back months.
September settled down 0.45 cent at 75.10 cents a lb, having ranged from 75.80 to 74.60 cents. November sagged 0.30 cent, to 77.20 cents, while the rest of the board closed 0.15 to 0.30 cent weaker.
An estimated 2,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official tally of 1,084 lots.
Technically, September support was pegged at 73.50 cents, followed by 71.30 cents. November support was seen near 76.00 cents.
Dealers said they expected the market to continue to trade quietly ahead of a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International, on August 14.
Meanwhile, traders largely brushed aside news that two Mediterranean fruit flies were found this weekend in Polk County -- the first to be discovered in an active commercial orange grove.

The flies turned up in an area where no medflies have been found previously and medfly fighters are worried they may be the first sign of an undiscovered infestation. If more flies are found in the area, they may resume spraying of malathion.

These medflies were the first to spotted in more than a week in Florida -- apart from the deliberately-released sterile medflies. The medfly fight has been largely turned over to the sterile flies, which are supposed to be mating with the survivors of the malathion to make sure they produce no offspring before they die.
